extracted.intended_audience: USPTO personnel (examiners, CRU/TC staff) and patent practitioners (patent owners, third-party requesters)
extracted.subtask_short: ex parte reexamination and prior-art citation
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance from the MPEP on filing, processing, and deciding citations of prior art and ex parte reexamination requests (content, timing, service, processing, decisions, certificates). Targeted to USPTO staff and practitioners who prepare or respond to citations and reexamination requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of Prior Art (35 U.S.C. 301; 37 CFR 1.501)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent may cite patents or printed publications believed to have a bearing on patentability; an explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying such prior art to at least one claim is required and the citation and explanation will become part of the patent file. At the written request of the citer, identity may be excluded from the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation must show pertinency/applicability to at least one claim (a broad statement of pertinency is minimum); patent-owner citations may explain how claims differ from the art. Citations entered in the patent file except as set forth in rules (see §§ 1.502, 1.902).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Cite Prior Art / Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Any person’ may submit prior art citations (individuals, corporations, government entities, patentees, licensees, requesters, persons without a real interest, or agents). A requester may ask in writing that their identity be excluded and kept confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential citers should not identify themselves anywhere in papers; include at least an unsigned statement that the patent owner has been sent a copy (or, if service impossible, file a duplicate). Complete assurance of exclusion cannot be guaranteed because review is mainly clerical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for Filing Prior Art Citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations may be filed 'at any time' defined by rule (37 CFR 1.501(a)) as any time during the period of enforceability of the patent (term + six-year statute of limitations per 35 U.S.C. 286). If litigation is instituted within the statute period, citations may be submitted after expiration so long as the patent is still enforceable against someone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations submitted after an order to reexamine will not be entered until reexamination terminates unless they fall into enumerated exceptions (e.g., submitted by patent owner or by requester with required fee/documents). To be considered without paying another reexamination fee, third-party art must be presented before reexamination is ordered (compliance with 37 CFR 1.501). Purpose: prevent harassment by frequent submissions during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Requirements for Prior Art Citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions under 35 U.S.C. 301 are limited to written prior art consisting of patents or printed publications and must include an explanation of how the cited art is pertinent and applicable to at least one claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred to include copies of cited patents/printed publications and necessary English translations; at minimum indicate how each cited item shows or teaches at least one limitation of at least one claim. Identify target patent by patent number, issue date, and patentee; use a cover sheet with identification and attach all documents. Affidavits/declarations (e.g., commercial success) may accompany citations. No fee required for submission under 37 CFR 1.501. Do NOT include issues not directed to patents/printed publications (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 112, public use, conduct of patent owner); such submissions should be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service / Certificate of Service / Duplicate Copy Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations by the public should either reflect that a copy was mailed to the patent owner at the correspondence address or, if service is not possible, be filed in duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All third-party citations must indicate service on patent owner or include duplicate copy with explanation why service was not possible. If duplicate is filed, send duplicate to patent owner when notifying entry; if no duplicate, provide notification without a copy and make original available for copying by patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Prior Art Citations (TC Responsibility and Entry Timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Technology Center that examines the class/subclass of the patent must determine immediacy of entry, whether the citation meets statutory/rule requirements, and enter it into the patent file at the appropriate time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proper and filed prior to an order in any pending reexamination, enter into patent/reexamination file immediately. If filed after an order and not entitled to entry under reexamination rules, retain (store) in TC until reexamination concludes, place an e‑tag reminder, and do not consider it during the reexamination. Notify patent owner (and sender/third-party requester as appropriate) if citation is stored or entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing When Citation Does NOT Qualify for Entry
rubrics_metrics.description: If the citation is improper (not limited to patents/printed publications or lacks the requisite citation description), it should not be entered and sender (if known) and patent owner should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling varies by whether service of copy was included and whether the sender is known; original or duplicate copies may be returned, sent to patent owner, or discarded as appropriate. Patent owner filings that are improper should be returned with notification; after an order for reexamination, patent-owner submissions go under the appropriate reexamination rule (1.555 or 1.933). Unusual issues should be raised to Office of Patent Legal Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Avoid Examiner-Initiated Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examiners should not, on their own initiative, place or forward prior art citations for placement in a patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are responsible for making patentability decisions; activity that appears to indicate claims are not patentable outside of cases pending before them is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question (SNQ) of Patentability — Criterion to Order Reexamination (37 CFR 1.515)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for ex parte reexamination will be granted (reexamination ordered) only if a substantial new question of patentability affecting at least one claim is found under the statutory/rule standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SNQ found (1.515(a)), reexamination ordered (1.525) and new examiner assigned; if not found, reexamination is denied/terminated. Requester may petition Director under 1.515(c) to review denial. The SNQ determination must be supported by prior art and explanations provided in the request (see guidance for request content).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Ex Parte Reexamination — Required Content and Supporting Papers (37 CFR 1.510)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester must submit a request containing identification of the patent, the fee, the prior art relied upon (patents/printed publications), and a statement applying the cited art to at least one claim showing why a substantial new question of patentability exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include copies of the cited prior art, a copy of the printed patent, a certificate of service (or show service/duplicate), and any affidavits/declarations necessary to explain dates or content. Use of transmittal form PTO/SB/57 is available but not mandatory. Incomplete requests are processed per MPEP and may be returned or given time to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and Translations of Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: It is preferred that copies of all cited patents or printed publications and any necessary English translation be included with a prior art citation so value can be readily determined by those inspecting the file and examiners during reexamination/reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of copies or translations can impede evaluation; provide full documents when possible. For foreign-language documents include an English translation or explain essential parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner Submissions and their Treatment (including 37 CFR 1.555 / 1.933)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations and submissions by the patent owner are entered in the file (including during reexamination) per the applicable rule (1.555 for ex parte; 1.933 for inter partes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proper, patent owner submissions are entered whether filed prior to or after an order; no notification to patent owner is necessary when they file. During reexamination, owner may submit evidence/affidavits to address issues such as nonobviousness or enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to Patent Owner When Third-Party Citation is Entered or Stored
rubrics_metrics.description: When a third-party citation is entered into the patent file (or stored because filed after an order for reexamination), the patent owner (and sender, if known) should be notified of the action and whether the citation will be considered in an ongoing reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification letters should state whether the citation was entered or retained in storage, identify the patent and reexamination control number if applicable, indicate whether the sender was confidential/identified, and advise the patent owner of options (e.g., submit art under 1.555 during reexamination or requester may file a reexamination request). Examples of notification wording are provided in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and Assignment of Reexamination Requests (CRU/TC Procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial processing is done in the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) or Technology Center (TC): determine completeness, assign reexamination if ordered, open reexamination file, assign examiner, and manage record systems and transfer procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place e-tags for stored citations, follow specified PALM/IFW status codes, complete checklists (PTO-1516 examiner, PTO-1517 clerk), and ensure certificate changes are correctly entered when reexamination matures to certificate. Reexaminations ordered at Director’s initiative follow same handling flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Considered and Prior Art Basis for Decision on Request
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to order or deny reexamination is based on the patent claims (as they exist at the time) and on the prior art cited in the request and the explanations demonstrating how that art raises a substantial new question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reexamination of a reexamination is filed, consider claims as modified by any previously issued reexamination certificate (enter certificate changes as preliminary amendment). Include copies of any prior reexamination certificates when deciding subsequent requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Actions — Form, Content, Time for Response in Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: During ex parte reexamination, the examiner issues office actions in accordance with the rules (e.g., 1.104) addressing patentability of claims; office actions may be final or non-final, and set time periods for patent owner response or amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel review is conducted at each examination stage (except non-merits informality notices). The flowchart shows procedures for non-final action, final rejection, reopening prosecution, patent owner responses under 1.111/1.113/1.116, and notices of intent to issue reexamination certificate. Examine whether an office action is final; allow response periods and extensions per rules; use specific PTOL forms (e.g., PTOL-466 Office Action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Owner Statement and Third-Party Reply (37 CFR 1.530, 1.535)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reexamination is ordered, the patent owner may file a statement addressing the reexamination (timing per rules); a third-party requester may file a reply under specified rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner statement and any third-party reply are considered by the examiner; timing and page/format requirements are governed by the cited rules. Third-party replies may be limited to specific opportunities (e.g., after owner statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Procedure in Ex Parte Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner can appeal a final decision in reexamination by filing a Notice of Appeal and appeal brief; examiner's answer, appeal conference, Board decision, and possible further appeals to CAFC or civil action are available per procedural rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flowcharts indicate sequence: Notice of Appeal (41.31), Appeal Brief (41.37), Appeal Conference, Examiner’s Answer (41.39(a)), Reply Brief (41.41(a)), possible Board decision under 41.50 (new grounds may reopen prosecution), rehearing requests, and appeal to courts (1.301/1.303 as applicable depending on filing date of reexamination). Use PTOL forms for notifying non-compliant briefs and other appeal-stage communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination Certificate — Numbering, Format, and Content (35 U.S.C. 307; 37 CFR 1.570)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reexamination is concluded with allowance of claims, the Office issues a reexamination certificate identifying the patent, the reexamination request number/date, prior art cited (those considered), and the status of claims (confirmed, canceled, disclaimed, or not examined). New claims are printed in italics; amended claims printed with italics and bracketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte certificates continue ordinal numbering; inter partes start a separate sequence. The certificate INID fields mirror patents (title, inventor, classes, abstract). Certificates are associated with the e-copy of the patent in search files and distributed to depository libraries and exchange foreign offices. Certificate numbering encodes whether it's B- or C-kind and the reexamination count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concluding Reexamination Proceedings — Modes and Processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexaminations may conclude by denial, vacatur, termination (no certificate issued), issuance of a reexamination certificate (1.570(b)), merge with reissue (1.570(e)), or merge with inter partes (1.997(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When denied/vacated/terminated, process file for appropriate PALM/IFW status and partial refunds per 37 CFR 1.26(c) as applicable. When certificate issued, follow processing in MPEP §2287 and review by CRU SPE or TC QAS before OPLA processing. Merging with reissue/inter partes has special processing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening Rights Resulting from Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amended or new claims determined to be patentable in reexamination have intervening-rights consequences analogous to reissue (section 252 analogies); 35 U.S.C. 307 addresses certification of patentability/unpatentability and claim cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP references case law and explains that rights for prior users/makers/importers/substantial preparers prior to certificate issuance are governed similarly to reissue intervening rights. Examiners and practitioners should consider intervening-rights implications when claims are amended/confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination of a Reexamination — How to Evaluate Requests and Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request is filed on a patent for which a reexamination certificate has already issued (or issues while a later request is pending), the new request must be considered based on the claims as modified by the previous reexamination certificate, not on the original claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reexamination file should incorporate certificate changes before examiner action; examiners must ensure the certificate changes are properly entered; preliminary amendments (certificate) should be included in order/denial decisions for subsequent requests. Amendments that re-add certificate text as if new are improper; notify patent owner via Form PTOL-475 to correct defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Affidavits/Declarations with Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations, or other written evidence may accompany prior art citations to explain content or pertinent dates (e.g., commercial success affidavits tied to a particular prior art document).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may submit affidavits to raise nonobviousness or to question enablement of cited art. Such documentary evidence must be limited to explaining patents/printed publications or clarifying dates—not used to introduce issues outside permitted scope of 35 U.S.C. 301 citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Forms for Ex Parte Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific PTO forms must be used in ex parte reexamination actions and processing (PTOL-471 grant/deny request; PTOL-466 office action; PTOL-467 advisory action; PTOL-468 notification re appeal; PTOL-462R notice of defective appeal brief; PTOL-304R advisory after filing appeal brief; PTOL-469 notice of intent to issue certificate; PTOL-465 communication transmittal; PTOL-474 interview summary; PTOL-475 notice of defective paper; PTOL-473 communication; PTOL-1517 reexamination clerk checklist; PTOL-1516 examiner checklist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Request for Ex Parte Reexamination Transmittal Form (PTO/SB/57) is available on the USPTO website for filing but is not mandatory. Use the listed forms for the corresponding processing steps to ensure uniform handling and compliance.
